m5-t1.question: What turns a normal chat model into a custom assistant?
options: A persistent configuration: instructions, knowledge files, capabilities, conversation starters and sharing settings
m5-t1.explanation: GPTs, Gems, Projects and Agents are all the same idea: a saved configuration around a chat model.

m5-t1.question: Which behaviour rule is TESTABLE?
options: Ask one question at a time and wait for the answer before explaining
m5-t1.explanation: Concrete, observable rules can be checked in a test plan; vague adjectives cannot.

m5-t1.question: What should the instructions say about uncertainty?
options: Explicitly permit 'I don't know' and forbid inventing formulas, sections or figures
m5-t1.explanation: Uncertainty behaviour must be written in, or the model will fill gaps with plausible inventions.

m5-t1.question: Which group belongs in an assistant test plan alongside happy-path, edge and knowledge-boundary prompts?
options: Adversarial prompts that try to break the rules
m5-t1.explanation: Adversarial tests ('ignore your instructions…') reveal guardrail weaknesses before real users do.

m5-t1.question: Before sharing an assistant publicly you should NOT:
options: Keep personal data in its knowledge files
Name an owner and a feedback channel
Test it link-only with a few users
m5-t1.explanation: Personal data in knowledge files of a shared assistant is a privacy breach.

m5-t1.question: A custom study assistant may answer only from a course syllabus. Which instruction is important?
options: Cite syllabus sections and say when the answer is not in the supplied material
m5-t1.explanation: A bounded assistant should cite its approved knowledge and abstain when evidence is absent.

m5-t1.question: A study assistant starts answering questions about financial aid outside its intended scope. What guardrail helps?
options: Define the scope, provide an approved hand-off route and test out-of-scope prompts
Give it more conversation starters only
m5-t1.explanation: Scope and fallback instructions prevent overreach.

m5-t1.question: A custom assistant uses an outdated handbook. How should its owner fix the root cause?
options: Tell users to ignore every date
Ask the model to guess which version is newest
Replace or version the source and test that citations point to the current approved document
m5-t1.explanation: Knowledge needs an owner and version control.

m5-t1.question: A placement coach asks users to paste full identity documents into a public assistant. What should its builder change?
options: Promise that public tools never retain data
Minimise collection and direct users to share only approved, necessary information
m5-t1.explanation: An assistant should collect the minimum data needed and respect tool controls.

m5-t1.question: A model gives different advice in two identical sessions. What feature improves repeatability?
options: Stable instructions, source versioning and a test set of representative prompts
m5-t1.explanation: A controlled setup and evaluation set make changes detectable.

m5-t1.question: A conversation starter asks “Tell me your password so I can help.” What should the owner do?
options: Keep it if the assistant is private
Remove it and prohibit collection of secrets
Ask users to change passwords afterward
m5-t1.explanation: Assistants should never solicit passwords or secrets.

m5-t1.question: A custom assistant is shared with an entire college. What should be tested before launch?
options: Whether the maker likes the icon
Role, permissions, source access and behaviour for unintended users
m5-t1.explanation: Shared assistants need access and abuse testing.

m5-t1.question: A user asks a course assistant for an answer that is missing from its documents. Which behaviour is safest?
options: State the gap, avoid guessing and point to a human or official source
m5-t1.explanation: Abstention and escalation prevent invented policy.

m5-t1.question: A builder changes instructions but does not test existing examples. What risk follows?
options: A fix for one prompt may break previously working behaviour

m5-t1.question: A student adds a copyrighted textbook to a personal assistant and shares access publicly. What should they check?
options: Permission to upload and share, tool terms and access restrictions
Whether the textbook cover is visible
Nothing if the assistant is free
m5-t1.explanation: Source rights and sharing scope must be reviewed.

m5-t2.question: What does RAG do when a question arrives?
options: Retrains the model on your documents
Retrieves relevant passages from your documents and makes the model answer from them with citations
m5-t2.explanation: Retrieval-augmented generation grounds the answer in retrieved passages rather than the model's memory.

m5-t2.question: Where do most RAG failures originate?
options: The documents (scans, poor headings, giant files) and the question wording
m5-t2.explanation: Ingest/chunk problems and mismatched question wording cause most misses — and you control both.

m5-t2.question: Which document preparation step helps retrieval most?
options: Descriptive headings, one topic per section, real text (OCR), versions dated
m5-t2.explanation: Retrieval works on passages; clear, well-labelled, text-based sections are found reliably.

m5-t2.question: In the grounding test, what should happen for a question NOT covered by the documents?
options: The assistant invents a plausible answer
The assistant says it cannot find it in the sources
The assistant searches the web silently
m5-t2.explanation: Honest boundary behaviour is a core test criterion; invention means the system is not trustworthy.

m5-t2.question: Why must you click citations even when they are present?
options: Because a cited passage does not always support the sentence attached to it
It is required by the licence
m5-t2.explanation: Cited is not the same as correct — verify that the passage says what the answer claims.

m5-t2.question: A RAG assistant cites a paragraph from an irrelevant handbook chapter. What should be checked first?
options: Retrieval chunking, metadata and whether the selected passage actually supports the question
m5-t2.explanation: Retrieval can return text that is close but not relevant.

m5-t2.question: A handbook was revised but the retrieval index still contains the old version. What is the failure?
options: A perfect model refusing to answer
m5-t2.explanation: RAG depends on current sources and a maintained index.

m5-t2.question: The assistant returns a citation but the cited sentence does not support its conclusion. What should the evaluator record?
options: A successful answer because there is a citation
A grounding failure: citation presence is not evidence support
m5-t2.explanation: Citations must be checked for semantic support, not just existence.

m5-t2.question: A RAG system retrieves only the first page of a long policy. Which improvement may help?
options: Use meaningful chunking with overlap and preserve section metadata
Ask the model to fabricate missing sections
m5-t2.explanation: Chunk design and metadata affect retrieval quality.

m5-t2.question: A question is not answered by the supplied handbook. What should a well-designed assistant do?
options: Infer a policy from common practice
Abstain clearly and route the user to an authorised office
Ask the user to trust its judgement
m5-t2.explanation: RAG should not turn missing evidence into invented policy.

m5-t2.question: A team wants to measure retrieval quality. Which test is useful?
options: Ask the model whether it retrieved correctly
Create questions with known source passages and check whether the right evidence is retrieved
m5-t2.explanation: Ground-truth questions reveal whether the system finds relevant evidence.

m5-t2.question: A notebook answers fluently using only three uploaded documents. What limitation remains?
options: The notebook must know every external fact
Source grounding proves the documents are current
Citations remove the need for review
The answer can be incomplete if the corpus is incomplete or poorly curated
m5-t2.explanation: Grounded answers inherit omissions and errors from their sources.

m5-t2.question: A team uploads student records to a research notebook. What should it assess?
options: Whether the service is approved, what data is retained and whether the task can use de-identified data
Whether the notebook can summarise quickly
m5-t2.explanation: Data handling controls apply to document-grounded tools too.

m5-t2.question: The same term appears in two policies with different meanings. What should the source setup preserve?
options: Document title, date, section and context so users can distinguish versions
A single answer with no citations
m5-t2.explanation: Metadata helps retrieve and interpret the correct passage.

m5-t2.question: A user asks a RAG assistant for legal advice beyond the handbook. What is the correct boundary?
options: Generate a legal conclusion from memory
Explain the source limitation and refer the user to a qualified authority
Offer a guarantee based on one passage
m5-t2.explanation: A document assistant should not overclaim beyond its evidence and role.

m5-t3.question: Which block starts an automation run?
m5-t3.explanation: A trigger (new form response, schedule, new email) begins each run; actions follow.

m5-t3.question: How should AI steps inside automations be designed?
options: Narrow, structured (JSON or fixed labels), validated by a filter, templated for external content, data-minimised and logged
m5-t3.explanation: Nobody watches each run, so outputs must be constrained and checkable.

m5-t3.question: What is the safest way to test a flow that sends emails?
options: Send to the full contact list
Filter to your own address until the flow is proven
Test in production on a weekend
m5-t3.explanation: Runaway sends are a classic failure; test with yourself as the only recipient.

m5-t3.question: What is a 'silent failure' and how do you prevent it?
options: A step failing unnoticed for weeks; prevent with an error handler that notifies you and a periodic run summary
A slow run; upgrade the plan
m5-t3.explanation: Error handlers and run summaries make failures visible.

m5-t3.question: Which platform is highlighted as open source and self-hostable with no per-run cost?
m5-t3.explanation: n8n can be self-hosted, which suits privacy-sensitive or higher-volume flows.

m5-t3.question: An automation’s AI step sometimes returns malformed JSON. What should the workflow do?
options: Send the malformed output to every user
Validate the schema, retry or route failures for human review before downstream actions
Assume the model will fix it later
m5-t3.explanation: Structured outputs need validation and a controlled failure path.

m5-t3.question: A trigger watches a spreadsheet row and sends a student notification. What should be checked before activation?
options: Whether the AI can write a poem
The number of staff in the department
Trigger conditions, test cases, permissions, duplicate behaviour and message content
m5-t3.explanation: Automations need end-to-end tests before they create real side effects.

m5-t3.question: An AI step returns a student’s personal details in a public Slack channel. What was likely missing?
m5-t3.explanation: Sensitive data must not flow to an audience that should not see it.

m5-t3.question: A scheduled automation runs each day, but yesterday’s task failed. What observability should exist?
options: A hidden spreadsheet with no timestamps
Logs, status, error alerts and a responsible owner who can retry safely
No record to protect the automation
m5-t3.explanation: Monitoring and ownership make failures visible and recoverable.

m5-t3.question: A workflow posts a draft announcement without approval. Which design change fits?
options: Add another generative step after posting
Insert a human approval step before publication
m5-t3.explanation: External publication is a consequential action that should be approved.

m5-t3.question: A low-code flow gets rate-limited by a provider. What is a responsible response?
options: Queue work, back off safely and notify an owner rather than dropping or duplicating actions
m5-t3.explanation: Rate limits require safe retry and queue management.

m5-t3.question: A prompt-based step extracts invoice totals. What output should be validated?
options: Currency, numeric type, required fields and reconciliation against the source document
Whether the output has a polite greeting
m5-t3.explanation: Financial extraction needs deterministic format and source checks.

m5-t3.question: A flow has a manual correction step but no record of who approved it. What is missing?
options: An audit trail for review decisions and ownership
m5-t3.explanation: Approvals should be attributable and reviewable.

m5-t3.question: A team wants to compare Make and n8n for an institutional workflow. What matters beyond price?
options: Hosting, data access, control, maintainer skills, audit needs and exit options
Which has the newest launch video
m5-t3.explanation: Tool selection must include governance and long-term ownership.

m5-t3.question: A workflow uses an AI classification to route complaints. What should happen to low-confidence or sensitive cases?
options: Send them to a defined human review queue
m5-t3.explanation: Uncertain and sensitive cases need accountable review.

m5-t4.question: What is the first step in improving a business process?
options: Mapping the process as it actually happens, with times, hand-offs and errors
m5-t4.explanation: You cannot improve what you have not seen; the swimlane map reveals waste.

m5-t4.question: Which scorecard criterion is reverse-scored?
m5-t4.explanation: High risk lowers the score: external, irreversible or legal impact argues against full automation.

m5-t4.question: A task scores 20/30 on the scorecard. The recommended action is:
m5-t4.explanation: 17–23 → automate with a human checkpoint; 24–30 automate now; 10–16 augment; below 10 leave or fix the process.

m5-t4.question: Which human-in-the-loop pattern suits external, irreversible actions like sending a quote to a customer?
m5-t4.explanation: Approval gates belong where errors are costly and cannot be undone.

m5-t4.question: Why does the one-page proposal end with a two-week pilot?
options: People approve a limited trial with a success measure far more readily than a permanent change
m5-t4.explanation: A bounded pilot with a decision date lowers the perceived risk of saying yes.

m5-t4.question: Staff report that a written procedure differs from daily practice. Which source should the process map capture?
options: The actual workflow, including informal hand-offs, exceptions and failure points
m5-t4.explanation: Improvement starts from how work really happens.

m5-t4.question: A task saves 30 minutes but errors could trigger an incorrect fee notice. How should risk affect automation?
options: Add a human checkpoint and measure both time saved and error consequences
Automate immediately because time savings are large

m5-t4.question: An automation scorecard rates tasks on value, effort and risk. Why reverse-score risk?
options: Higher risk should reduce the recommendation to automate without controls
Risk has no relation to the task
m5-t4.explanation: Risk should lower suitability unless mitigated.

m5-t4.question: An external quote is generated automatically. Which approval pattern is appropriate?
options: No review if the prompt is detailed
Human before send, because the action is external and hard to reverse
m5-t4.explanation: Approval before an irreversible external action is the stronger control.

m5-t4.question: A two-week pilot has no success measure. What should the proposal add?
options: A promise that staff will like it
A list of every AI provider
A baseline, numeric target, owner, risk controls and decision date
m5-t4.explanation: A bounded pilot needs a measurable decision rule.

m5-t4.question: A process includes many exceptions. What should happen before automating the common path?
options: Document exception types and route them safely rather than silently dropping them
Send each exception to a public tool
m5-t4.explanation: Exception handling is part of the workflow design.

m5-t4.question: A department measures automation success only by messages sent. What is a better measure?
options: Task completion quality, error rate, time saved and user impact
m5-t4.explanation: Operational outcomes are more meaningful than activity counts.

m5-t4.question: Staff spend four hours reformatting AI output. Is the workflow successful?
options: Yes, if the AI output was long
Not necessarily; include correction and review effort in the ROI calculation
No, because all AI tools are bad
m5-t4.explanation: ROI should include end-to-end effort and quality.

m5-t4.question: A business process changes every month. What should an automation owner plan?
options: A maintenance owner, change review and safe rollback or pause process
m5-t4.explanation: Automations require lifecycle ownership and adaptation.

m5-t4.question: A process touches personal records and a public chatbot. What should the redesign consider?
options: Data minimisation, approved systems, access control and retention before automation
The colour of the approval button
m5-t4.explanation: Governance is part of process design, not a later add-on.

m5-t5.question: People need to enter, view and update structured records with different roles. What should you build?
m5-t5.explanation: Forms, lists, detail screens and permissions are what no-code app builders provide.

m5-t5.question: What should be designed FIRST in an app?
options: The data: tables, typed fields, owners and visibility
m5-t5.explanation: Screens are built on tables; changing data later forces rebuilds.

m5-t5.question: How should an AI feature behave inside a no-code app?
options: Suggest, be editable, be labelled as AI-suggested, and have a fallback value
Run on every row every minute
m5-t5.explanation: AI should help a human decide, with visible, overridable output and a sensible failure state.

m5-t5.question: Why test the app logged in as a second, lower-privilege account?
options: To check row-level visibility rules — where beginners leak data
m5-t5.explanation: Permissions bugs are invisible when you test only as the owner.

m5-t5.question: Which is part of a responsible hand-over?
options: Transferring ownership to an institutional account, a privacy notice, an owner, and a retirement rule for data
Keeping the app on your personal account forever
m5-t5.explanation: An app without an owner, notice and retirement rule becomes a liability.

m5-t5.question: A no-code app stores student profiles. What data decision should come before screen design?
options: Define data fields, owners, access rules and retention
Add every field that might be useful someday
m5-t5.explanation: Data structure and visibility are core design decisions.

m5-t5.question: An app’s AI assistant suggests a fee reminder. How should the suggestion appear?
options: As an official payment demand without review
Clearly labelled as AI-suggested, editable and reviewed before sending
m5-t5.explanation: AI assistance should remain visible, editable and subject to human checks.

m5-t5.question: A student account can view another student’s records. What test would catch this?
options: Test only as the app owner
Ask the model whether privacy is correct
Sign in as a lower-privilege second account and verify row-level access
Check that the home screen loads
m5-t5.explanation: Permission testing must use accounts with different access.

m5-t5.question: An app uses an external AI API. What should happen when the API is unavailable?
options: Show a clear fallback, preserve user work and route unresolved items for review
m5-t5.explanation: Graceful failure preserves safety and trust.

m5-t5.question: A no-code builder creates an app from a prompt. What remains the builder’s responsibility?
options: Validate data, permissions, functionality, privacy and accessibility before use
Nothing, because the builder is automated
Ask AI to approve the launch
m5-t5.explanation: Generated code or configuration still needs human testing.

m5-t5.question: A form collects birth date although the app only sends event reminders. What principle suggests removing it?
m5-t5.explanation: Collect only data needed for the stated purpose.

m5-t5.question: A builder uses a personal account to own an app for a college. What handover is appropriate?
options: Share the password with all staff
Transfer ownership to an institutional account and name a maintainer

m5-t5.question: A user submits an empty form and the app’s AI crashes. What should the test plan cover?
options: Malformed inputs and a safe error response
m5-t5.explanation: Realistic tests include malformed data and error conditions.

m5-t5.question: A student-facing app displays generated advice as if it were a policy. What should change?
options: Label suggestions, cite approved policy, provide a contact and avoid inventing rules
m5-t5.explanation: Users should know which content is generated and where to verify official rules.

m5-t5.question: Before launching an app to a pilot group, what is important?
options: Launch to everyone and see what happens
Test with representative users, verify permissions, publish a privacy notice and define a rollback owner
m5-t5.explanation: A controlled pilot tests both usefulness and safeguards.

questions.question: A custom assistant will answer questions from a college handbook. Which setup is strongest?
options: Upload every available file and tell it to answer confidently
Curate current approved documents, define scope and citation behaviour, and instruct it to abstain when the answer is absent
Use a broad web search instead of the handbook
Hide the source files from reviewers
questions.explanation: A reliable assistant needs curated sources, a bounded role, traceable citations and an abstention path.

questions.question: A handbook assistant cites the correct document but quotes an obsolete section. What failed?
options: The source corpus or version metadata was not controlled; update and label authoritative documents
The model used retrieval, so the answer must be current
The user prompt was too polite
The citation format was too short
questions.explanation: RAG is only as reliable as its document selection, versioning and retrieval.

questions.question: A Make automation sends fee reminders directly to students. Which action should require approval?
options: Sending an external message that could expose incorrect balances or personal data
questions.explanation: External, consequential and difficult-to-reverse actions should have a human approval checkpoint.

questions.question: A workflow trigger fires twice after a network retry. How should the system avoid duplicate messages?
options: Add another AI step to decide whether it has sent
Use an idempotency key or processed-status check before the send step
questions.explanation: Idempotency prevents duplicate side effects when a job is retried.

questions.question: A process scorecard rates automation value high but risk-if-wrong very high. Which recommendation fits?
options: Fully automate because the total score is high
Keep a human checkpoint or approval gate because high error impact dominates the decision
Ignore the scorecard and launch immediately
Train the model on more examples and remove review
questions.explanation: High risk calls for a human-in-the-loop control even when potential value is attractive.

questions.question: A no-code app has role-based student records. What is the most important test before launch?
options: Sign in as a second lower-privilege account and verify row-level visibility and write permissions
Check the colours on the login page
Ask the builder AI whether security is enabled
Test only as the app owner
questions.explanation: Testing with a lower-privilege account catches cross-user data exposure.

questions.question: A custom assistant is moved from a student’s personal account to a college workflow. Which hand-over matters most?
options: Keep the personal account as the permanent owner
Remove all documentation to simplify support
Let the assistant approve its own updates
Transfer to an institutional owner, document approved data and retention, assign a maintainer and define retirement
questions.explanation: Institutional ownership and lifecycle responsibility are essential for a sustained system.

questions.question: A small RAG pilot gives cited answers to handbook questions but fails on missing policies. What should the assistant do?
options: Invent a likely rule and cite the closest section
Search unrelated public sites without telling the user
Say the supplied documents do not answer, route the case to the office and log the gap
Repeat the question until an answer appears
questions.explanation: A safe knowledge assistant abstains on missing evidence and provides a human route.

questions.question: A college wants to automate a process, but staff disagree about the actual steps and exceptions. What comes first?
options: Map the current process, hand-offs, exceptions, time and failure points with the people doing the work
Ask a model to infer the process from the policy
questions.explanation: Understand the process as it actually operates before designing automation.

questions.question: An AI step is unavailable during a student-support workflow. What is a responsible fallback?
options: Use a reviewed template or queue for human follow-up, log the failure and avoid fabricating a response
Send the last generated answer again
questions.explanation: Graceful degradation preserves service and accountability when AI fails.
